risks.title: The executive performance test treats any database URL that contains localhost or a test marker as disposable, seeds the first organization it finds and leaves the rows behind
preconditions: An operator sets EXECUTIVE_PERF_DB to a URL that satisfies the substring test but reaches a real database: a local port forwarded to a remote database, or a marker placed in a query parameter or a user name.
The operator runs the dedicated performance script, which is never part of the ordinary test run or of continuous integration.

evidence.note: The script that runs the suite names the dedicated configuration and nothing that limits the target.
The only guard is an unanchored regular expression applied to the whole URL string.
Teardown only closes the connection; no statement removes the rows the run wrote and none counts them.
The first organization of the target database, by identifier, receives the seeded customers; the suite creates no organization of its own.
A dedicated configuration selects only the suite that writes; the ordinary configuration excludes it.

existingControls: The suite is skipped unless EXECUTIVE_PERF_DB names a database, and the ordinary test configuration excludes it, so neither a normal run nor continuous integration reaches it.
A URL that contains none of the permitted substrings is refused before any write.
controlGaps: The permitted substrings are matched anywhere in the URL, so a forwarded port to a real database, an application-name parameter or a user name satisfies the guard.
The run seeds the first organization of the target database and creates no organization of its own.
Nothing removes the seeded customers afterwards and nothing proves that they are gone.
No test feeds the guard a deceptive URL.
acceptanceCriteria: A test asserts that the performance suite connects only to a database that the harness itself created for the run, and refuses any URL it did not create.

A test asserts that the host and the database name are compared against an exact allowlist and never by substring, so a URL that carries localhost in a query parameter, a user name or a path is refused.
A test asserts that a tunnel or a production-like target is refused: a loopback address with a forwarded port to a remote database, and a database named like a production one.
A test asserts that the suite seeds an organization fixture of its own and never selects the first organization it finds.
A test asserts that teardown removes every row the run created and that the run counts the fixture's rows afterwards and fails if any remain.
A test asserts that deceptive URLs are refused: a user-information trick, a query string, an upper-case host, a trailing dot, and an IPv6 loopback with another port.
risks.residualRisk: A refused target protects the database the variable names. It does not protect a database an operator deliberately builds from production data, and it does not remove the customers already written by an earlier run.

findings.summary: No role can assign OWNER and transfer_ownership has no implementation, so an organization's OWNER is effectively immutable through the API.
remove_member is OWNER+ADMIN and no last-OWNER invariant was found in the route, so an ADMIN removing the sole OWNER would leave the organization with no holder of the 13 OWNER-only permissions.
view_erp_compensation exists in the permission table while enforcement uses a direct role comparison: two sources of truth for one rule.
delete_org is declared with no implementation, so whether organization deletion is intended to exist is undecided.
The empty-success ratio across the inventory: 163 call sites and 96 consumer edges answer an outage with an apparent success.

Published cases are served to anonymous graph and operations endpoints from the in-process ring during an outage; published-only, so not a disclosure, but the public graph can misrepresent the estate.
The silent majority: 211 of 392 call sites carry no logging on their degraded path.

Brute-force detection is lost during an outage: no counter, no login.failed event and no lockout state are recorded, and the isAccountLocked fail-open is masked only because issueTokens throws and the handler answers 503.
Public certificate verification answers HTTP 200 with the holder name "Unknown" during an outage: it mis-attributes rather than mis-validates.

Telemetry ingestion answers an industrial gateway HTTP 201 Created with ingested: 0 when the readings were dropped, so the gateway neither buffers nor resends, and a TELEMETRY_INGESTED audit row asserting count 0 is attempted and fails on the same outage.

The site filter is skipped on the industrial graph route when the client is null; latent only because loadOrgGraph returns null on the identical condition, and cross-tenant exposure is impossible because organizationId is filtered unconditionally.
Organization, billing, knowledge and platform-key writes answer a database outage with HTTP 422 while echoing an internal "Database unavailable" reason string.
Compliance writes answer a database outage with HTTP 409, and the export-download path writes an EXPORT_TOKEN_REPLAY_DENIED audit row for what was an outage.

A billing webhook the platform could not durably claim is answered HTTP 200 with outcome IGNORED, so the provider treats the event as delivered and never retries, and the WEBHOOK_REJECTED row fails on the same outage.

changeMemberStatus does not check revokeAllSessions' result, so a partial failure between the suspension write and the generation bump can leave a suspended member's non-organization sessions live until expiry.
Dead write paths exist whose refusal nothing can observe.
A response payload carrying an isFallback field sets it to false on a fallback.
Health functions report zeros instead of unknown when they could not ask.
Usage metering records are dropped silently during an outage.
initiatePasswordReset cannot signal its own failure.
The case, knowledge and analysis write responses assert storageMode "database" while the write went to process memory: the client is told which store it went to, and that statement is false.

Five academy routes report an outage as HTTP 401 "Authentication required" because a local resolveUser helper collapses four distinct conditions into one null, while a sixth route answers 200 with a null stats block for the same condition.

Gateway revocation answers HTTP 404 "Gateway not found or already revoked" while the credential stays valid, with the GATEWAY_REVOKED audit event written only after the guard, so an operator responding to a suspected compromise is told the job is already done.
The gateway heartbeat route writes a GATEWAY_HEARTBEAT audit event and meters the call after touchGatewayHeartbeat returned early without persisting anything.

The industrial and twin update paths map an outage to HTTP 404 "not found" while their create siblings answer 503, and two relation and tag creators answer 422 "may be duplicate" — an outage reported as a unique-key violation.

Twenty-seven consumer edges and nine exported functions have no caller in src/ or scripts/, including the whole of the site-membership module, so site membership can neither be read nor managed through the product.

The document tenant repository redirects a zero-row update to the in-process store, so a PATCH for an id present in neither store still answers as a successful update; deliberate and tenant-filtered, but the one in-memory write on that surface that is not an outage path.
119 of 124 exception edges are silent; only five log.

Silent database-to-session fallback in six core repositories plus one document path: 69 fallback points, 34 inside bare catch blocks, writes included, zero logging, so any transient Prisma exception reroutes a mutation into process memory and reports success.

The industrial and twin read paths answer an unavailable database with an empty success: 26 sites on the legacy single-line shape and 98 on the semantic definition, so an operator reads "zero alarms" when the truth is "no connection".
The archive list returns envelopes only, but the detail page renders the stored snapshot, built under a synthetic OWNER scope with every axis and every site, without narrowing it to the reader.

The customer project route returns recorded project cost per currency, summed from the cost ledger, to any holder of view_erp (OWNER and ADMIN), although the ERP layer shows cost only to the compensation holder (OWNER).

POST /api/executive/reports/run accepts the dedicated token, the metering token or the metrics token; the comment that says the dedicated token excludes the others is not what the code does, and the pass response and cursor carry other tenants' organization ids.

The new worker service declares env_file for the whole production environment file, as the three earlier workers do, so the image-level 'no credential' property does not bound what the running process holds.
If the worker's batched settings read throws, every organization falls back to the default zone and the pass stores an immutable report for that zone's night.
If the release of the notification claim cannot be performed, the claim stays set and the archive records an announcement nobody received, with no later retry.
A pass with no database answers HTTP 200 like a held lease, a failed claim is reported as not claimed, and the detail page shows an unreadable archive as a missing report.

If the worker's single read of an organization's active sites throws, the empty list becomes the industrial section's site list, the section is stored as FORBIDDEN (no site granted), and the immutable report is never corrected because no product code calls the correction path.

All 27 ERP route files refuse a caller who lacks the platform admin capability before the organization permission is checked; the four customer route files and the customer pages check only organization permissions, so an organization OWNER or ADMIN who is not a platform admin reads linked-project data and changes a project's customer.

setProjectLink reads the project's current customer and then updates by id with no precondition and no row-count check, then writes a success audit event, so a concurrent link can overwrite another and both audit rows claim success.
Creating or renaming a customer checks for a clashing name with a read and then writes; the migration defines no unique index on the name, so concurrent requests can store duplicates.

ErpProject.organizationId is nullable, and a composite foreign key is not enforced when one of its columns is null, so the claim that a cross-tenant link cannot be stored holds only for rows with an organization.
The runner entrypoint accepts a platform-administrator session cookie but, unlike the sibling cookie-authenticated writes, does not call the trusted-origin guard.

Each stored report keeps a full snapshot as unbounded JSON, including the names of the users who acted on approvals and costs, with no retention or deletion rule other than cascade on organization deletion.
The pass selects every organization by id with no status or activity filter; the Organization model has no status field, so whether dormant organizations should be skipped is undefined and unproven.

An existing report is looked up by organization and date label only, and each pass targets only the last completed day, so a zone change can reuse a label for a different window and a night missed entirely is never reported.

The nightly pass writes a frozen financial snapshot per organization under a synthetic OWNER scope with no audit record, and no read of the archive is audited by the read module, by either archive page or by a database trigger; only a correction is audited and nothing issues one.

Customer contact data (Party) and the free-text contact log (PartyInteraction) are stored with no deletion, anonymisation, export or retention rule: the customer library has no such operation and neither model is in the closed erasure registry, the closed export registry or the processing inventory; customers are archived and interactions are append-only.

The nightly pass freezes a ranked priority list, built under the synthetic OWNER scope that now also holds the customers axis, and the archive detail page renders it without narrowing it to the reader.
A customer's display name is copied into the frozen priority list stored in the report row, a column that no erasure, export or retention registry names.

The executive performance test accepts any database URL that merely contains _test, _ci, localhost or 127.0.0.1, seeds the first organization of that database with customers, and has no teardown, so a local tunnel to a real database is treated as a throwaway one.
No host-level restriction exists on inbound 80/443: nginx binds 0.0.0.0 and ::, UFW is ALLOW IN Anywhere on both families, DOCKER-USER carries no allowlist, and Docker DNATs both ports publicly.
The original finding about the identity of 185.80.196.163 was withdrawn and superseded.
findings.reason: Withdrawn in S0: that address is on no interface of the production host, so the question is moot. Superseded by EDGE-05 (the drift that caused it); retained only so the withdrawal stays traceable.

findings.summary: ngx_http_realip_module is entirely unconfigured — real_ip_header, real_ip_recursive and set_real_ip_from are all absent from both nginx config files.

Two production files carry comments asserting the rate limiter fails open on an unknown action when it fails closed, misstating a safety property in the dangerous direction; one already caused an error in a committed security document.

deploy/nginx/default.conf lists a stale address in server_name while the host's address is different — harmless as a matching token, but a false statement about the deployment embedded in configuration, and the direct cause of one invalid audit test.
The claim that a Cloudflare-fronted response arrives on the origin's own address was reclassified as test-environment interference and the identifier retired.
findings.reason: Reclassified in S0 on the origin self-check: the real origin answers with nginx's signature and no Cloudflare headers, so the premise was false. The identifier is retired and was deliberately not revived by the 2026-10-11 independent-vantage evidence, which is recorded under EDGE-09 and EDGE-10 instead.

findings.summary: x-powered-by: Next.js is present on the origin response — framework disclosure on every response.
A HEAD request, nominally side-effect-free, returns Set-Cookie NEXT_LOCALE with a one-year Max-Age; this is next-intl's documented locale negotiation and carries no identity.

The origin is reachable directly from the public internet: a request from a vantage independent of both the production host and the audit environment was answered with the origin's own signature and no Cloudflare headers, so the edge can be bypassed from outside.
Routing to the origin address was unstable between two observations 23 seconds apart from the same device; both observations are genuine and the mechanism is not established.

The IP pseudonymisation salt can be silently absent: SHA-256(ip + process.env.JWT_ACCESS_SECRET) with no check, while jwtSecret() accepts three other variable names, so a deployment setting only JWT_SECRET salts with the literal string "undefined".
POST /api/auth/access-request has no idempotency or duplicate suppression; the rate limiter is the only bound on repeated rows.
POST /api/sales/leads uses a module-local in-memory Map as its limiter instead of the shared Redis limiter, so the counter resets on restart and each replica enforces its own cap.

POST /api/candidate/register has no schema validation: a hand-written interface plus raw JSON.parse, so email is never validated as an email and name, phone, location, skills and workAuthorization are unbounded.
POST /api/candidate/register answers 409 "Email already registered", a direct account-existence oracle that contradicts the platform's stated anti-enumeration posture.
user.create and createCandidate are not in a transaction, so a failure between them leaves a candidate-role User with no candidate record.

The three public media handlers borrow the Copilot demo's rate-limit buckets (copilot-demo-get / copilot-demo-post), so one public feature can exhaust another's allowance and neither can be tuned independently.

The one trusted header carries nginx's peer address, which behind Cloudflare is an edge PoP; resolveClientIp's own premise ("no Cloudflare") is false and the mitigation its comment prescribes was never applied.
CF-Connecting-IP arrives on every request, is neither stripped nor rewritten, and is read by no code: the correct value is available and discarded.
Neither IP extractor normalises: IPv6, IPv4-mapped, bracketed and port-bearing forms key differently, and a missing header collapses every caller into one "unknown" bucket.
Two independent IP extractors exist with no shared code, so a fix to one does not reach the other.
The salt guard is an un-propagated fix: the media view beacon names the other two call sites and their line numbers, calls them "same secret, same algorithm", and adds the guard only to itself.
ArticleView.ipHash has no writer anywhere in src/.
A wrong input IP makes all three ipHash columns pseudonyms of a PoP — still non-reversible, but no longer the personal datum they are governed as, and useless for attribution.
isPayloadSessionActive returns true for any payload without a sid, with no storage-mode guard and no defence in depth on the read side; the protection lives entirely on the mint side.
A change of HERMES_STORAGE_MODE to session takes effect on the next recreate, redeploy or restart, after which logins issue sid-less unrevocable cookies; startup check W7 warns but does not block.
Legacy cookies minted before Phase 91 carried no sid and closed through the 30-day absolute iat ceiling rather than through any revocation.
findings.reason: Phase 91 has long been deployed and the 30-day SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS ceiling has since elapsed, so no such cookie can still verify. It is retained as the shape that recurs on any future credential-format change, which is carried by R-02's acceptance criteria rather than as a live risk.

findings.summary: verifySession enforces signature and absolute age but never consults the session store, so all revocation force comes from the single sid branch in isPayloadSessionActive.

signSession and verifySession key off AUTH_SECRET alone and fall back to a constant published in this repository with no NODE_ENV guard; the FATAL startup checks evaluate a different resolution order, and the one check naming the constant is a WARNING that does not fire when AUTH_SECRET is merely absent.

Public certificate verification returns the holder's real name with no rate limit, and the verification token's entropy cannot be established because nothing in src/ writes it — there is no mint site in this repository.
adminSeed() makes a standing environment-driven privileged account whenever ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD are present.

The middleware matcher excludes /api and any dotted path, so none of the 572 API handlers receives middleware authentication, and there is no central authorization choke point: 572 handlers are 572 independent enforcement decisions.
No role can assign OWNER and an ADMIN cannot even assign ADMIN; all three places that accept a client-supplied role clamp it, and the clamp is a recorded fix for a real prior defect.

The AuditLog model is a plain append table with no previousHash, hash chain, signature, append-only enforcement or WORM retention, and its organizationId, outcome and correlationId columns are all nullable.

No SAST, secret scanning, container or image scanning, IaC scanning, DAST, SBOM generation or artifact signing appears anywhere in the 13 workflows; the only dependency control is the dependency-audit gate.

The compliance organization-scope helper, used by 35 route files, refuses on an unverifiable token, a revoked session, an unavailable database, an ambiguous membership and a missing active organization, and resolves the organization server-side from membership rows.

The production compose file carries none of read_only, cap_drop, security_opt, no-new-privileges, tmpfs or resource limits, no seccomp or AppArmor profile, and its internal network is a plain bridge rather than internal, so containers retain outbound egress.
Because the Content-Security-Policy is set in middleware and middleware excludes /api and dotted paths, API responses and static uploads carry no CSP.

Six /api/customers handlers serve a customer-success book of business — company names, plans, ARR, health scores and renewal risk — to the anonymous internet with no authentication, authorization, rate limiting or audit, backed by 17 static records naming real companies.
The migration role and the runtime role are not separated in anything found in S0: one connection string holds both.
Database connection encryption is not configured in the repository: sslmode is absent from both example environment files.
The development compose file publishes the PostgreSQL and Redis ports, uses a weak default database password and sets no Redis requirepass at all.
Signed document export tokens have a time-to-live and a download route exists; the value and the re-authorization behaviour on download were not verified in S0.
The backup, restore, blue-green and envelope-encryption machinery is substantial, and S0 executed none of it: no backup was taken and no restore was performed.

The 26 ERP route files apply four gates in order with an origin refusal on every write, and the ERP data layer raises a controlled 503 so no raw Prisma error reaches a caller and no ERP path degrades to in-process storage.
The getPrisma classification document states 79 selftests in one section and 75 in two others after the corrective revision updated only the first.

The proxy forwards the health path on the insecure port with access logging switched off, while every other path on that port is redirected, so requests to the health surface leave no proxy access record.

Strict-Transport-Security is set nowhere: both nginx configs contain zero add_header directives, next.config.ts states HSTS is set exclusively by nginx, and the header was confirmed absent on a production response and again on the direct origin response.
No container image is digest-pinned: all four are floating or semantic tags, including the Node base image and nginx:alpine.

Two committed S0 documents record opposite statuses for one precondition: the legacy-token document calls the signing-variable precondition unverified, while the edge document records the owner-supplied presence check and the verdict that the flaw is not active in the observed container.
There is no account-level MFA, TOTP or WebAuthn implementation: the only one-time-code code is a candidate application-withdrawal flow, not account authentication.
The tenant contract records, as established fact in product source, that six module data layers query Prisma with no organizationId predicate although every root model declares the column.

No library in the dependency tree can speak OPC UA, MQTT, Modbus, S7, BACnet, PROFINET or EtherNet/IP, so no code path from Hermes reaches a PLC, HMI, historian or OT network; industrial data enters only through the signed gateway-envelope surface.
No PostgreSQL row-level-security policy was found: tenant filtering is entirely caller-side.
The DR secret-scan script walks generated JSON manifests so they cannot carry a secret value; it never examines the source tree or git history.
findings.reason: The same absence seen from the other side: it explains why the one script whose name suggests secret scanning does not provide it.

findings.summary: The billing organization resolver uses findFirst with orderBy createdAt asc, so for a user in two organizations it silently picks one.

The gateway envelope is canonicalised length-prefixed in a fixed field order rather than by serialising caller input, compared with a timing-safe comparison, and carries timestamp, nonce and idempotency key inside the signed field set; no Prisma model stores key material.
Whether one gateway's secret can be used against another gateway's identifier depends on secret-provider key separation, which was not verified in S0.

Gateway authentication is per-gateway HMAC with environment-resolved secrets; mTLS, per-device certificates, a certificate lifecycle, expiry monitoring and a dual-key validation window are all absent.
The Phase 99 attack-surface narrative states 355 route files, 497 handlers and 13 public writers while the committed inventory on this source state reports 412, 572 and 14.
Both argon2 and bcryptjs are in the dependency set; which is authoritative for new passwords, and whether a bcrypt verification path remains reachable, was not established in S0.
The 135 handlers classified as platform-administrative were not re-audited handler by handler and are explicitly not asserted correct — only not contradicted.
Every request crosses from the proxy to the application as plain traffic on a bridge network, with no identity between the two hops.

No public handler returns another tenant's data and none accepts a tenant, user or role identifier from the client: every privileged column a public writer sets is hardcoded, and every public route file's rate-limit action is registered.
A re-authentication and step-up module is present; its scope and coverage were not established in S0.
The production compose sets Redis requirepass with a weak literal default when the environment variable is unset.
The Redis client sets no global key prefix or namespace and key construction is entirely caller-side, so whether every tenant-scoped key embeds an organizationId is unverified.
The cache has no transport encryption configured and relies on being in-network only.
Project guidance names a guard called requireActor that has zero definitions and zero uses, and the Phase 99 classifier still registers it as a guard token.
No incident runbook directory exists in the repository.
server_tokens off is absent from the nginx configuration.
The session store treats a missing row, a revoked row, an expired row or an unreachable database as revoked, and is documented Node-only so it is never imported from the edge.

Only 9 of 410 API route files reference a site-level guard, against 78 using the organization actor guard and 120 using the permission guard, and the schema carries 54 siteId references against 580 organizationId references.
The single-sign-on module is present and was not inspected in S0.
The inventory reports zero unauthenticated webhooks; the payment webhook's signature verification was not read in S0 and is explicitly deferred.

Twelve security-control dependencies — the session revocation check, the organization and site actor contexts, the login credential lookup, three entitlement reads, the AI-egress policy store, the academy request scope, the candidate retention check and two tenant-context readers — were each traced and confirmed to deny rather than to succeed emptily when the database is unavailable.

The uploads volume is mounted inside the application's public directory, so its contents are served as static assets with no authorization check and no CSP; filenames are 128-bit random, and the only two writers store images intended for public publication.

Each worker image contains exactly one dependency-free script with no node_modules, no ORM, no application code and no database credential, and a packaging test asserts the runner and migrator stages copy no scripts.

findings.summary: TENANT_ADMIN and OWNER_ONLY are declared vocabulary with no detector: classifyHandler cannot emit either value, so the reported zeros are a structural impossibility rather than a measurement.

requirePermission, present in 120 route files at 168 call sites, is registered at scope tenant, so every permission-gated handler flattens to TENANT_MEMBER regardless of how privileged the permission is.
Three OWNER-only permissions have no requirePermission consumer: two are unimplemented operations and the third is enforced by a different mechanism.
The ERP compensation boundary is enforced as a derived boolean in the repository layer, with no textual signature any token-matching classifier could detect.
The classifier's unit of counting is wrong for this codebase: privilege is per action, selected inside the handler from an ACTION_PERMISSION map, so one (path, method) pair spans three tiers.
The GUARD_TOKENS table is hand-maintained, lacks the two scopes its own output schema advertises, and contains a dead token for a guard that does not exist.

Negative-test coverage for unauthorised roles could not be assessed: the two targeted classifier tests could not be executed in this worktree, so this is absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence.
The sales-leads route uses a route-local in-memory limiter keyed on a collapsed IP: it resets on restart and multiplies per replica.
